A GUIDE TO THIS ATLAS

Start with the law.
Follow the source.

This is a curated starting point for AI research, not an exhaustive legal inventory. Coverage includes AI-specific statutes, automated decision-making, synthetic media, and selected privacy and consumer-protection laws relevant to AI. Entries link to primary legal sources or clearly labeled legislative research summaries. New York has an expanded research collection; depth varies by state.

“Enacted” confirms adoption; it does not mean every provision is operative or enforceable. “Upcoming” identifies adopted measures with future duties. “Guidance” identifies agency expectations rather than a newly enacted statute. Amendments, court orders, exceptions, and later developments may affect application. Local measures are labeled separately; proposals are not included in this collection.

The original state survey was checked on 18 September 2026. New York and the additions identified in California and Utah were checked on 22 September 2026. Each entry shows its source-check date. This collection does not update automatically or comprehensively track litigation. General federal, consumer-protection, civil-rights, and sector laws may also apply. Map colors describe the collection, not regulatory strictness.
